title: Privacy-aware sampled metrics export guardrails
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: console telemetry exports currently include fine-grained event metrics that, when combined with other datasets, can leak user-identifying patterns. We need a set of server-side export guardrails that reduce PII risk for analytics consumers while preserving product telemetry usefulness.

Goal: implement a privacy-aware sampled export pipeline for metrics and aggregated events that ensures: (1) deterministic, auditable sampling keyed to a hashed customer/session id so deletion and opt-outs can be enforced; (2) aggregation and suppression rules (thresholding) to avoid small-count leaks; (3) pluggable differential-privacy noise for select exports; and (4) export gating with audit logs and tear-down support for revoke/delete requests.

Scope: backend pipeline changes for Console analytics exports (Kafka -> aggregation layer -> export topics) and the export configuration surface in the Console backend. This ticket covers design, core implementation, and rollout plan; separate tickets will handle UI for export configuration and per-customer overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic sampling algorithm implemented and documented; sample decision derived from HMAC(customer_id, export_salt, window_id) and stored for the export window
Exported aggregates contain suppression: groups with count < configurable threshold (default 10) are omitted or bucketed into 'other'
Differential privacy module available as opt-in per-export with configurable epsilon; unit tests demonstrate expected noise profile
Deletion/opt-out: when a Delete request is received for a customer_id, past export windows that included sampled rows are flagged and an expunge manifest is generated for downstream partners
End-to-end integration tests that simulate export consumers verify no small-cell PII leaks in sampled exports
Performance: added sampling and suppression must not increase median export pipeline latency by more than 10% under normal load
implementation_notes: Sampling: use HMAC-SHA256 with a rotation-bound export_salt stored in KMS; compute sample_key = HMAC(salt, customer_id || window_id) and compare first N bits to sampling_rate threshold for deterministic selection
Windowing: align sampling windows to fixed 1-hour buckets (ISO timestamps) to make decision reusable across retries and idempotent for replayed events
Suppression: run group-by + count in the aggregation tier; drop groups where count < export.threshold or replace with SUMMARY_BUCKET; do not export raw low-count groups
DP noise: implement Laplace mechanism for numeric aggregates behind feature flag; document epsilon selection guidance and provide example conversions (epsilon -> expected error) in design doc

Deletion handling: maintain tombstone index of windows that included a customer_id for 90 days; generate downstream expunge manifest (s3/manifest_{export}_{date}.ndjson) and emit audit event console.export.expunge
Auditability: write per-window sampling decisions and suppression audits to an append-only audit topic (Kafka, retention 180d) with encrypted payloads; add schema version field
Backfill: backfills must be marked as backfill=true and use a different salt to avoid accidental inclusion of historical per-customer sampling decisions; partner contracts must be notified
Rollout: start with internal-only exports -> selected pilot customers -> global opt-in. Export configuration will default to sampling=false for existing exports unless opted-in
Migration: provide a compatibility mode where we publish both old and new export topics for 4 weeks to allow consumers to migrate
Monitoring: add Grafana panels for sampled export rates, suppression rate, average group size, and audit topic lag
notes: Trade-offs: deterministic sampling simplifies deletion and auditability but can enable fingerprinting if sampling rate is high; recommend conservative defaults (1-5% for user-level exports) and clear consumer-level documentation
Legal: coordinate with Privacy Counsel before enabling exports to EU customers; DP is preferred for signal that will be used for cohort building
Failure modes: if KMS salt rotation is misconfigured, sampling decisions may shift — include a fallback to mark such windows as 'salt-rotation-affected' and refuse export until operator approval
Operational: ops runbook to rotate salt and re-vet expunge manifests; add CLI tooling to produce per-customer expunge manifests on demand
